findings.title: The surface fire-route summary says no listed pair fires the match by itself, and owner row 2 says firing needs a second fault at Q124; both are false for the PYRO1_OUT-to-3V3 (0.5135 mm) and PYRO1_OUT-to-3V3A (0.5662 mm) pairs, whose own rows give 0.3-0.8 A in the match with the bus enabled against the 0.75 A all-fire
findings.contradicts: docs/R10_VALIDATION.md line 2340 ('An OUT-to-GND bridge or a failed-short Q124 can fire an enabled match ... None of the pairs below fires the match by itself.') and owner row 2, line 2169 ('Firing still needs a second fault at Q124'), whose 'Row 2 residuals' (line 2219) include 'the other pairs of the §1 inventory'. They contradict the same file's rows at lines 2354-2355 ('With the bus enabled the bus feeds the 3V3 rail through R134 and the match (about 0.3-0.8 A ...)', 'As the row above, through R164 into 3V3A') and line 2390 ('roughly 0.3-0.8 A in the match against the J-Tek 0.30 A no-fire and 0.75 A all-fire'), REQUIREMENTS 'Igniters' row (maker 0.75 A all-fire / 0.5 s), and the I-5 mechanism the records accept (FMEA_REDUNDANCY line 37: battery voltage onto 3V3 can make the MCU drive PE4). The round 23 lens that added these two rows called them 'bus-enabled fire routes' (round23_safety.md R23-SAFETY-08 (b)). FMEA I-5's 'R10 routes' list and owner row 1's list of single faults that fire with the bus enabled leave them out.
findings.evidence: Board 92c3ad59, pcbnew shape distance (.supervisor/r26_safety/adjacency.py, adj_92c3ad59.json): PYRO1_OUT R173.1 to 3V3 D120.3, B.Cu, 0.5136 mm; PYRO1_OUT track (15.5,56.6)-(16.87,57.97) to 3V3A R164.2, B.Cu, 0.5662 mm (both unchanged since 5516eeec; diff of the two inventories shows no change). Physics (Calculation, with the records' own inputs): with PC1 high and Q124 off, a bridge connects the bus (BAT_IN 7.3-8.4 V through Q120/Q121, R134 2 ohm, leads <= 0.3 ohm and the 1-2 ohm match) to 3V3. U2 (AP63203) does not sink current in PFM (Diodes DS41326 Rev 3-2, 'Pulse Frequency Modulation': 'The buck converter does not sink current from the output when the output load is light and while the device is in PFM'), so 3V3 rises above regulation (past the MCU's 4.0 V absolute maximum, DS12110 Table 119) until the rail's loads and clamps absorb the current; the records put that current at 0.3-0.8 A, which reaches the 0.75 A all-fire. If the rail is held near 3.3 V instead, (7.3 - 3.3) V / (3.0-4.3 ohm) = 0.93-1.33 A, above all-fire. Either way one bridge with the bus enabled (the normal pad state after the on-rail check) can fire the match, directly or through I-5, without any fault at Q124. A pre-existing bridge is refused by the cold screen (CONT 0.295 V against 99 mV), as the row says; a bridge that forms after PC1 goes high is not.
findings.impact: The owner decision table and its supporting §1 tell the owner that the §1 surface residuals (row 2) cannot fire the match without a second fault at Q124. Two of them can, with the bus enabled on the pad. The owner's acceptance of rows 1 and 2, and the respin list (which names a 3V3 clamp but not these pairs), rest on that statement.
findings.concrete_fix: Docs only. In R10_VALIDATION §1 replace 'None of the pairs below fires the match by itself' with: 'Two pairs below can fire an enabled match by themselves: PYRO1_OUT to 3V3 (R173.1-D120.3, 0.5135 mm) and to 3V3A (R164.2, 0.5662 mm), 0.3-0.8 A in the match against the 0.75 A all-fire and bus voltage onto 3V3 (the I-5 class); the QSPI_IO2-PE4 pair needs a sustained IO2-high pattern; the rest do not.' In owner row 2 limit 'Firing still needs a second fault at Q124' to the load-switch, EN and sense-divider pairs, and add the two PYRO1_OUT pairs to owner row 1's single-fault list and to FMEA I-5's R10 routes (with the existing lever, owner row 18, and a respin option: R173 / D120 / R164 spaced >= 1 mm or a GND guard).

findings.title: The 'fire budget's four-stall BAT_IN of 5.73 V' is the value from before the AUX allowance; the bound budget gives 5.713 V, where the single drop-out is 8.07 ms (not 8.2) and the 100 ms window limit 7.50 ms (not 7.63), and the chatter test voltage sits 17 mV above the stated corner
findings.contradicts: m3_design/assembly_review/sources/r10_design/parts_budget.json (board-bound to 92c3ad59): fire_current_GAP1.primary_40mohm_FETs.pack_7V4_by_stall_count['4'].loaded_pack_V = 5.713189767224944 (fire_A 1.278747, the four-stall figure M3_R10 'Current fire budget' quotes). The records instead state: REQUIREMENTS F6 (line 60) 'only about 8.2 ms at the fire budget's four-stall BAT_IN of 5.73 V'; the generated binding note (r10_binding_note.json line 589, from m3_design/r10_sch_check.py line 295) 'about 8.2 ms at the fire budget four-stall BAT_IN of 5.73 V'; AGENTS §1 battery row, M3_R10 lines 270 and 591, R10_VALIDATION row 21 and the §4 C87 row, STATUS line 11 and REQUIREMENTS line 106 ('8.2 ms at the four-stall 5.73 V'); the bench rule 'U9 stays on for the whole run at 5.73 V (worst-corner limit 7.63 ms at 5.73 V)' in F6, ORDERING 8.3 line 617 ('run this test at 5.73 V'), REQUIREMENTS F4 ('which runs at 5.73 V'), the handoff line 68 and R10_VALIDATION row 21.
findings.evidence: Re-running the budget's own fire_case equation (r10_parts.py, current(7.4, 4)) with other_converter_load_W 13.064091 W gives 5.7132 V / 1.2787 A; removing the 100 mA AUX allowance (buck_max 5.5463 V x 0.1 A / 0.8 = 0.6933 W, D-R19-14) gives 5.7318 V / 1.2829 A, i.e. the '5.73 V' and the a3144b15 figure '1.282918 A at four stalls' that M3_R10 quotes as superseded. So 5.73 V predates D-R19-14; D-R19-10 / D-R20-11 / D-R24-19 / D-R25-01 carried it. Own worst-corner EN model (.supervisor/r26_safety/en_model.py; R80/R165 +1 %, R81 -1 %, C87 0.72 x 220 nF, 0.1 uA EN sink, D402 50 nA, VUVLO(F) 1.116 V, TI SLVSFC9C p9), which reproduces every recorded figure (8.204 ms and 7.629 ms at 5.73 V, 10.345 / 20.111 / 26.023 ms, 5.871 / 9.594 ms, the trip-fraction table, 1.0953 V and 1.0277 V counter-examples): at 5.7132 V the single drop-out is 8.067 ms and the one-block-per-100-ms limit 7.503 ms; the 7 ms rule still holds there (it holds down to 5.6465 V).
findings.impact: The quoted four-stall immunity and window limit are 0.13 ms too optimistic for the current budget, and the functional leg of the bench test ('U9 stays on at 5.73 V') runs above the corner it is said to represent. The 7 ms pass line itself stays correct at 5.713 V (0.50 ms margin, not 0.63 ms).
findings.concrete_fix: Restate the four-stall point from the bound budget: 5.71 V (5.713 V), single drop-out about 8.1 ms (8.07 ms), window limit 7.50 ms at 5.71 V, margin 0.50 ms; run the bench test at 5.71 V or lower. Change the chatter obligation text in m3_design/r10_sch_check.py (and its pin in tools/test_r10_check.py), regenerate the binding note, and update REQUIREMENTS F4 / F6 / line 106, ORDERING 8.3, AGENTS §1, M3_R10, R10_VALIDATION rows 21 and §4, STATUS and the handoff; record it as a D-R26 decision.

findings.title: The '5.37 V four-stall-plus-fire corner' subtracts the fire current a second time from a four-stall point that already includes it; the budget's model gives 5.71 V with a healthy match and 5.50-5.56 V with a shorted match
findings.contradicts: Firmware rule 8 in m3_design/r10_sch_check.py line 322 and r10_binding_note.json line 615, M3_R10 line 1029, REQUIREMENTS F6 (line 60) and R10_VALIDATION owner row 25 (line 2202): 'below the 5.37 V four-stall-plus-fire corner'. Its derivation (round23_power.json R23-POWER-01: 'lowest legitimate BAT_IN 5.37-5.54 V at four stalls plus a fire pulse (7.4 V EMF, 0.15 ohm source, 5.73 V four-stall point; shorted match 2.26-2.41 A, healthy match 1.24 A)') is 5.73 - 0.15 x 2.41 = 5.37 V and 5.73 - 0.15 x 1.24 = 5.54 V; but the 5.73 V 'fire budget four-stall BAT_IN' is the pack voltage while the budget already feeds the fire branch (parts_budget.json fire_current_GAP1 cases carry fire_A with loaded_pack_V).
findings.evidence: Same equation and inputs as the budget (7.4 V EMF, 0.15 ohm, four 1.92 A stalls, 13.064 W constant-power load; .supervisor/r26_safety, python one-off recorded in the report): healthy match (branch 4.4678 ohm) 5.7132 V / 1.279 A; shorted match at hot R134 (2.4678 ohm) 5.5576 V / 2.252 A; shorted match with cold R134 and copper (2.4015 ohm) 5.5483 V / 2.31 A; match and 0.3 ohm leads both shorted, cold (2.1015 ohm) 5.4991 V / 2.62 A. None reaches 5.37 V: at 5.37 V the pack would have to supply (7.4 - 5.37) / 0.15 = 13.53 A, about 0.87 A more than even the match-and-leads-shorted case draws (12.67 A). The recorded healthy-match end (5.54 V) is not even equal to the four-stall point it starts from.
findings.impact: Wrong figure in a firmware obligation and the owner row. It is conservative for the PA6 window (the true corner is 0.13-0.34 V higher, VLOGIC about 5.35-5.56 V after U9 and U11), so no decision changes; but the window's 5.2 V top edge, and with it the post-trip hold-up, is bounded by a corner that does not exist.
findings.concrete_fix: Replace '5.37 V four-stall-plus-fire corner' with the budget-consistent corner: BAT_IN about 5.71 V with a healthy match and 5.50-5.56 V with a shorted match (shorted leads and cold R134 included), VLOGIC about 5.35-5.56 V (Calculation, fire_current_GAP1 model). Fix it in m3_design/r10_sch_check.py rule 8 (regenerate the binding note), M3_R10 rule 8, REQUIREMENTS F6 and R10_VALIDATION row 25.

findings.title: The §1 surface-inventory row calls U11.5 'OV2'; U11.5 is TPS2121 OV1 (IN1 = USB_LIMITED), and OV2 (pin 4) is tied to GND
findings.contradicts: docs/R10_VALIDATION.md line 2350: 'RAW_ACT sense branch to the USB_OVLO track | 0.175 mm | 7.4-8.4 V on U11.5 (OV2), above its 6 V absolute maximum'. TI SLVSEA3F (Aug 2020) Pin Functions p4: VQFN-HR pin 5 = OV1 ('Active Low Enable Supervisor for IN1 Overvoltage Protection'), pin 4 = OV2. The schematic symbol (r9_input/schematic.net.xml lines 8609-8610: pin 4 OV2, pin 5 OV1) and the same file's line 1584 ('U11 ... OV1 trip 5.76-6.27 V') agree with the datasheet.
findings.evidence: Board 92c3ad59 netlist (pcbnew): U11.5 = USB_OVLO (R87 47 k from USB_LIMITED, R88 10 k to GND), U11.4 = GND, U11.7 = USB_LIMITED (IN1), U11.2 = RAW_PROTECTED (IN2). The bridge figure itself reproduces: RAW_ACT chamfer (22.8,63.535)-(22.46,63.875) to the USB_OVLO track (22.0,64.75)-(22.5,64.25), B.Cu, 0.1772 mm on 92c3ad59 (0.175 mm on the labelled earlier board).
findings.impact: Wrong pin name in a safety inventory row; the stated consequence (7.4-8.4 V above the 6 V OVx absolute maximum, SLVSEA3F p6) is the same for OV1, so no conclusion changes.
findings.concrete_fix: Change 'U11.5 (OV2)' to 'U11.5 (OV1, IN1's USB over-voltage input)'.

observations: Chatter rule (D-R25-01) confirmed at the stated corner: own model reproduces 7.629 / 5.871 / 9.594 ms, the single drop-outs, the trip-fraction table and both counter-examples; a corner search over every +/- combination (incl. C87 0.72 / 1.0 / 1.27) confirms that corner is worst for single drop-outs and for the window; the latest-placement periodic train is the worst window-feasible train (300 random window-feasible trains at 7.0 ms: min EN 1.13301 V vs 1.13295 V periodic).

The '4000-train search under 7.62 ms kept EN >= 1.1173 V' is a sample result, not a bound: the periodic 7.62 ms / 100 ms train reaches 1.1162 V (still >= 1.116 V); the 7.629 ms limit itself is right. Not counted.

The chatter worst corner excludes resistor TCR, which the Pack row counts: with the fitted +/-100 ppm/K at a 70 C bay the window limit is 7.31 ms at 5.73 V and 7.18 ms at 5.713 V, still above 7 ms; the 7 ms line fails only above about 96 C (5.713 V) / 114 C (5.73 V) resistor temperature, outside the bay assumption; resistor temperature is disclosed as unqualified.

The window rule treats the contact as binary: a steady contact resistance above about 241 kohm trips a worst-case U9 at 5.73 V with no open time (5.73 x 297 / (1246.4 + Rc) - 28 mV < 1.116 V); the open/closed threshold is not stated. F9's 7 uA dry-contact qualification covers contact resistance. Suggestion only.

Per-flight step 3: J121.2 < 0.1 V comes about 0.2-0.3 s after J400 opens (EN <= 57 ms worst at 8.4 V, logic run-down, then C120 x 50 kohm, 63 ms) and 'no telemetry / no buzzer' within about 0.2 s, inside 1 s. The step-2 alternative 'TP81 and 3V3 below 0.3 V' may take 0.9-1.35 s (C84 back-feeding RAW_PROTECTED through U11 below IRCB, as R20-PWR-03 assumes, until TPS2121 VUV(F) 2.4-2.7 V, then R92 alone on about 74 uF; Inference: AP63203 UVLO falling 2.86-3.26 V). Fail-safe direction and Inference-dependent; TP81 / C15 face the sled on the rail. Not counted.

Hold-up after the PA6 trip (D-R25-02) reproduced: 0.103-0.164 / 0.291-0.430 ms and 0.22-0.31 of the break-to-3.8 V hold-up (constant power 11.249-13.064 / 4.295-4.650 W at 300.8 uF); 100-220 uF gives 0.034-0.120 ms from the trip. PA6 = VLOGIC / 11 (R60 100 k / R61 10 k on the board) as step 3 checks.

OVLO corner (D-R25-03) reproduced: (1.223 + 0.1 uA x (2.002 M || 279.72 k)) x 8.157 = 10.1764 V; R92 bleed 10.1764 V / 3.234 kohm = 3.147 mA; U9 bound 3.743861 A, margin 0.202327 A to 3.946188 A (TI 3.96 A at 750 ohm, SLVSFC9C p9). Lowest OVLO trip about 9.38 V, above a full 8.4 V 2S. No per-flight step depends on it.

REQUIREMENTS F4's option 'a flight-2 pack that holds >= 5.96 V under four stalls' rests on the single-drop-out reasoning D-R25-01 replaced (trains add up); harmless because ORDERING 8.3 requires the window test regardless. Not counted.
Pack change: TP80 below 1 V within 1.51 s worst (R167 10.1 kohm, <= 70.5 uF on BAT_IN incl. C89 / C95 through R166), inside the 2 s wait.
First-article ramp window reproduced: turn-off 4.288-4.802 V, turn-on 4.723-5.250 V, nominal 4.505 / 4.960 V; turn-on delay 30.3-130.3 ms (nominal 87.7 / 55.5 / 44.7 ms).

AGENTS §2 on the board: Q124 R126 220 ohm series, R128 10 k pull-down, C126 220 nF gate-source, R127 1 k at PE4 (U1.3); Q120 / Q121 R121 10 k series, R119 // R120 50 k to the common source, C120 1 uF gate-source; Q122 R122 1 k, R123 2 k, C123 10 nF (PC1 = U1.16); RAW_ACT reachable from BAT_IN only through Q120 D-S and Q121 S-D (back-to-back body diodes); all default off with PC1 / PE4 Hi-Z. Confirmed.

Single-fault sweep (19 protected nets, every copper layer, 0.6 mm; adj_92c3ad59.json): bus-on with J400 open via ACT_DRV / ACT_GATE to GND fills (0.2506 mm), Q121 gate-drain (0.520 mm) or a Q121 / Q122 short; board on with J400 open via the EN pairs of row 24 or a U9 IN-OUT bypass (U9.5 / U9.6 0.200 mm; In2 RAW_PROTECTED 0.2506 mm from the BAT_IN via (17.5,87.15)); fire with the bus on via OUT-GND (0.1768 / 0.1800 mm), C128, Q124, QSPI_IO2-PE4 and R26-SAFETY-01's pairs. All but the last are disclosed classes screened by steps 2-3 or the cold screen.

Adjacency diff 5516eeec -> 92c3ad59 over the same 19 nets: only ACT_GATE-BAT_SW_SOURCE left the 0.6 mm band (chamfer) and RAW_ACT-USB_OVLO went 0.175 -> 0.1772 mm; D-R24's copper added no hazard pair.

BUZZ_OUT (LS120.2, 3V3 through the coil) to the ACT_EN_MCU run 0.520 mm (D-R18-03's 0.5 mm floor): a bridge holds ACT_EN about 2.2 V with PC1 Hi-Z and enables the bus; disclosed class (row 2, PC1 enable chain); the cold screen sees BUS live.
(c') BAT_FAULT_N-ACT_EN_MCU 0.550 mm gives ACT_EN <= 0.554 V against AO3400A VGS(th) min 0.65 V, a 25 C figure; at a hot pad Q122 could conduct. R19 noted the 25 C basis; class disclosed.
S-8 re-measured on 92c3ad59: 12 barrels on 6 nets; PYRO1_OUT via 1.0209 mm to its GND partner, 1.0500 mm at the ACT_GATE vias, BAT_ENABLE vias (In2), J121.1 and J400.2; J121.1 In2 3V3 1.0613 mm.
ORDERING 8.3 chatter bullet repeats 'under flight-level vibration' twice (wording).
